passage:
The city library has a garden on its roof. From the street, people cannot see it. But on the roof, there are flowers, small trees, and benches.
The garden helps keep the building cooler in summer. It also gives insects and birds a place to rest. Visitors can go there after reading, but they must stay on the paths.
A student group visited the roof for a science report. They measured the temperature on the roof garden and on a nearby concrete roof. The garden was cooler.
One student said, "I thought a roof was just the top of a building."
The librarian answered, "It can be more than that if we use it carefully."
